Ifn /iDemoriam.
SAMUEL GOODALE (Theta "36).
The Convention records the obligation of the Fraternity to Samuel Goodale
(Theta '36), a founder of Psi Upsilon, who died at Columbus, Neb., Decem
bers, 1898. For almost two generations this honored and venerable brother
loved and served the Fraternity. He saw it grow from seven to a myriad,
and as it waxed greater and stronger his interest and affection for it seemed to
increase. His frequent presence in our chapters, clubs, conventions and so
cial gatherings was always welcome and benign, the more because, to the very
last, his eye was not. dimmed nor his natural force abated. Steadfast in the
faith of his coUege days, unswerving through his long life in zeal for the
honor and welfare of Psi Upsilon, the name of Samuel Goodale will be forever
held in living and fraternal remembrance.
The Committee on New Business reported General Resolutions Nos. 5 and
6, which were, under suspension of the rules, unanimously adopted.

Whereas, It is the sense of this Convention that the need of greater and
more uniform secrecy, more dignity and less ostentation, should be impressed
upon the members of this Fraternity,
Resolved, That it be the office of every campaign committee of the different
chapters to make this a point of discussion each year, and that in addition the
initiates be instructed in regard to their dignified behavior toward Fraternity
affairs.

THE COMMUNICATION OF THE EXECUTIVE COUNCIL TO THE
CONVENTION OF 1899.
I. Mbmberbhip. The active membership of the Fraternity on February 1,
1899, was 513, a decrease of 30 since the report of 1898. A table of member
ship is annexed.
II. Petition for New Chapter. The fifth petition from Kappa Gamma
Chi, St. Stephen's College, Annandale, N. Y., is herewith presented to the
Convention.
III. In Memoriam. Samuel Goodale (Theta '36), a founder of the Frater
nity, died December 8, 1898, at his home in Columbus, Nebraska, and the
Council submit herewith a minute of his services to Psi Upsilon. The Fra
ternity also lost by death during the year :
May 13, 1898, William Stevens
Perry (Alpha '65), Bishop of Iowa ; July 4, 1898, Edward Irwine Walter
(Phi '68), Professor of Romance Languages and Literature at Michigan
University, lost on La Bourgogne ; March 3, 1899, Nathaniel H. Clement
(Zeta '63), late Justice of the Supreme Court of New York, Second Depart
ment ; March 18, 1899, Othniel 0. Marsh (Beta '60), Professor of Paleontology,
Yale University ; March 27, 1899, James Ormsbee Murray (Sigma '50), Dean
of Princeton University ; April 5, 1899, Daniel Lord, Jr. (Lambda '66), senior
member of the law firm Lord, Day & Lord, New York City ; and May 5,
1899, Charles Henry Payne (Xi '56), D.D., LL.D., Secretary of the M. B.
Church Board of Education. Each name will recaU the sterling and attractive
qualities that endeared our deceased brethren to the Fraternity, and won for
them, in varied fields of labor, positions of trust and honor.
IV. The New Catalogue. Pursuant to General Resolution No. 3, of
1898, the Council have begun the preparation of the Eleventh General Cata
logue of the Fraternity, which will contain the names, addresses and occupa
tions of living members, and the dates of death of deceased members, arranged
by chapters and classes, the symbols of initiation, and, so far as possible, the
public official positions held by members; and, alphabetical and geographical in
dexes. Mr. CUnton H. Macarthy, of Brooklyn, N. Y., has been engaged to com
pile the material for the catalogue, under the divection and supervision of the
Council, and to attend to all the details of proofreading and presswork until the
books are ready for delivery. His work is to be finished by April 1, 1900. He is
to receive for his services $750, exclusive of disbursements for
stationery, print
ing and postage, estimated $5S50, As the chapters are aware, the selection of

11
Mr. Macarthy, who is not a Psi Upsilon man, has been criticised by the mem
bers of one of the chapters. The reason for his selection and the views of the
Council on the subject have been expressed in recent communications to the
chapters, but the Council will be pleased to furnish to the convention such
other information as may be desired. The following chapters have already
submitted their membership lists for the use of the compiler : Sigma, Gamma,
Psi, Xi, Iota, Pi, Chi, Beta Beta, Eta, Tau, Mu, Omega. Return postals are
now being sent out to verify names and addresses, and to secure further data
for the catalogue. It is earnestly hoped that the remaining chapters will im
mediately furnish their membership lists, so that necessary inquiries may be
prosecuted and the matter tabulated and ready for the printer at an early day.
There is a vast amount of detail work to be done, but if the chapters co
operate heartily with the Council the catalogue can be completed on time,
and without unnecessary expense. The estimated expense of printing and
binding the catalogue is $3,000.
V. Revision ov the Constitution. The Committee on Revision of the
Constitution submit herewith the result of their labors. It will doubtless be
impossible, in the brief life of the Convention, to discuss and deliberate upon the
changes proposed ; but if the Convention so direct, copies of the proposed re
vision will be prepared by the Council and forwarded to the chapters for their
consideration. The members of the Committee, other than the Council, were
George Henry Fox (Upsilon '67), Ira A. Place (Chi '81) and Norman S. Dike
(Sigma '85). The vacancies caused by the death of Daniel G. Thompson and
the election of George S. Coleman to the Council were not filled.
VI. Safekeeping of Records. For the permanent safekeeping of rec
ords and convenient access thereto the Council have rented a fire-proof room
in one of the best storage warehouses of New York, and, so long as available
space remains, tender it to the chapters for the preservation of any property for
which they may not have frequent use. In the constantly changing member
ship of the Fraternity, records, letters, programmes and other memorabilia are
lost or mislaid which, if preserved, would become of the greatest interest and
value. The Secretary of the Council will at any time furnish shipping and
other directions, and the Council commend to the chapters the advantages
thus offered.
VII. Visitation of Chapters. The Council regret that they have been
unable to visit many of the chapters during the past year, but are fully con
vinced of the wisdom of the plan contemplated by General Resolution No. 13
of 1895 ; believing that in no way can complete mutual understanding and
sympathy between chapters and council be more effectively maintained.

ant to General Resolution No. 3, of 1898, a tax was levied upon the chapters
at the rate of |3 for each active member on the rolls on February 1, 1899, for
the purposes of the new
catalogue.
Respectfully submitted,
Herbert L. Bridgman,
Francis S. Bangs,
William M. Kingslet,

The Fifth Application of the Kappa Gamma Chi of St. Stephen's Col
lege TO the Psi Upsilon Fraternitt.
St. Stephen's College,
Annandale-on-Hudson, N. Y., April 10, 1899.
To the Executive Council of the Psi Upsilon Fraternity.
Gentlemen: �
We beg to present to you the application of the Eappa
Gamma Chi of St. Stephen's College, for a charter of Psi Upsilon.
We come to you for the fifth time, confident that if we can make plain to
you, as we know it, the devoted interest of the members of the Kappa Gamma
Chi in this project and the unabated zeal that still animates them, we shall be
able to secure the charter which we so earnestly desire.
We have before this urged the point that the college is an institution of
general culture and training, and is not a technical school.
We have presented to you the record of our alumni, and the active share
which our undergraduates have in the college life.
Notwithstanding the fact that the college has lost its President, the Rev.
R. B. Fairbairn, D. D., LL. D., who had been at the bead of the institution
for thirty-five years, it has maintained its full vigor, and a still larger life and
growth is looked for with the administration which will soon be inaugurated
upon the election of a new President.
Again, we beg your careful attention to our claims, and respectfully ask
that a charter of Psi Upsilon be granted to the Kappa Gamma Chi of St.
Stephen's College.
(Signed) Alexander H. Vinton, D. D.,
Worcester, Mass.
John Aspinwall,
Barrytown, N. Y.
A. Randolph B. Hegeman,
Albany, N. Y.
Angus McK. Porter,
St. Stephen's CoUege.
